title: CDF bounds imply a Lévy distance bound
statement: For measures $mu$ and $nu$ on $bbr$, define their Lévy distance as the infimum of all $deltage0$ such that, for every $uinbbr$, $(nu((-infty,u-delta]).toReal-delta)lemu((-infty,u]).toReal$ and $mu((-infty,u]).toReallenu((-infty,u+delta]).toReal+delta$. If $epsilonge0$ satisfies these two inequalities with $delta=epsilon$ for every $u$, then the Lévy distance from $mu$ to $nu$ is at most $epsilon$.
hypotheses_covered: μ and ν are measures on ℝ
For every real u, ν's CDF at u−ε minus ε is at most μ's CDF at u
For every real u, μ's CDF at u is at most ν's CDF at u+ε plus ε
